clue.text: The Shakespearean jester's criterion

definitions.meaning: the court fool in As You Like It bears this name
a standard against which things are judged, originally a stone for testing gold

explanation.surface: A question about what standard Shakespeare's clown uses to judge things.
explanation.definitionFit: The fool in As You Like It carries the name, and the word also means a test stone for gold, hence any standard.

clue.text: Remaining throughout

definitions.meaning: left behind, as in food left ... after a meal
all through, as in famous all ... the world

explanation.definitionFit: Left-over things are remaining, and 'all over' means throughout an area or period.

clue.text: We hear its pukka seafood

definitions.meaning: pukka said aloud in British speech sounds like pucker, to wrinkle or crease, a sense of the answer

explanation.surface: Someone claims, by hearsay, that a dish of seafood is genuine and first-rate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'We hear' tells you the first definition is a sound-alike: pukka (Hindi-derived British slang for genuine) is pronounced like pucker, and the answer as a verb means to pucker or wrinkle.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb it means to wrinkle or pucker, as paper does when damp; as a noun it is an edible shellfish sold at British seaside stalls.

clue.text: Clothing that fits one to a T

parts.note: single means one, unaccompanied
the letter T, taken as written

explanation.surface: A garment said to fit someone perfectly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'To a T' looks like the idiom for perfectly, but here T is simply the final letter added after the word for one.
explanation.definitionFit: A sleeveless vest worn by athletes is an item of clothing.

clue.text: The shape the country's game is in!

definitions.meaning: England's national summer game, cricket, is played at the famous Kennington ground in London

explanation.surface: A rueful remark about what state the nation's sport is in.
explanation.walkthrough: THE OVAL is a London cricket ground where England play Test matches; the surface pretends to lament the state of the national game.
explanation.definitionFit: An egg-like outline is this shape, and the London cricket ground in Kennington bears the name.

clue.text: Overlooks cash spent abroad, a bad thing

parts.note: eyes means looks at or regards, as overlooks can mean to watch over
the ore is a coin of Sweden, Norway and Denmark

explanation.surface: Someone surveys money squandered overseas and judges it a mistake.
explanation.walkthrough: The ore is a small Scandinavian coin, one hundredth of a krona or krone.
explanation.definitionFit: Something ugly that spoils a view is an unsightly blot, a bad thing to look at.

clue.text: A pin from East Europe for feminine adornment

parts.note: a nail is a pin-like metal fastener
Polish means from Poland, in Eastern Europe

explanation.surface: A brooch pin from Eastern Europe worn as a woman's accessory.
explanation.definitionFit: Coloured lacquer painted on fingernails is a cosmetic decoration traditionally worn by women.

clue.text: Press a new head to make up the shortage

indicators.note: new letters are made by putting these words into a fresh order

parts.note: a ness is a headland, a promontory

explanation.surface: Printers press a new headline to fill a gap in the page.
explanation.walkthrough: 'New' rearranges PRESS A into SPARSE; NESS is a headland, as in Loch Ness's neighbour Orford Ness.
explanation.definitionFit: Scarcity or thinness of supply is a lack, so the noun means shortage.

clue.text: Incline to drive quietly

parts.note: to ram is to drive or force hard
p is piano, the musical direction for quietly

explanation.surface: A tendency to drive a car without making noise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Incline' looks like a verb meaning tend to, but it is a noun: a slope.
explanation.definitionFit: A sloping surface joining two levels is a slope or gradient.

clue.text: Part of centre page re-edited

indicators.note: edited again, so the letters of the two words are put in a new order

explanation.surface: A section of a newspaper's middle page has been revised.
explanation.definitionFit: A proportion of a whole, expressed per hundred, is a share or portion.

clue.text: Older animals can hold the Spanish back

indicators.note: back means the whole assembled string is read from right to left
hold means the word for animals contains the Spanish article

parts.note: rats are animals
el is Spanish for the

explanation.surface: Elderly creatures manage to keep the Spanish at bay.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hold' puts EL inside RATS to give RELATS, which 'back' then turns round.
explanation.definitionFit: Bread or news that is less fresh is more stale, so older in that sense.

clue.text: Again entering a horse when so directed

indicators.note: entering means the word for again goes inside the horse

parts.note: a steed is a horse
re- is the prefix meaning again

explanation.surface: Entering a horse in a race a second time when told to.
explanation.definitionFit: Guided a vehicle or animal in a chosen direction, so steered means directed.

clue.text: Season's about over, so providing support

indicators.note: about means the season goes around the other pieces

parts.note: spring is a season
on, as in a row on or over money, means concerning
taken as written

explanation.surface: The season is nearly finished, so backing is being offered.
explanation.walkthrough: 'About' wraps SPRING round ON and SO; 'over' and 'on' share the sense concerning, as in a fuss over (on) nothing.
explanation.definitionFit: Backing a team or event with money is supporting it financially.

clue.text: To take the fare in doorways appeals

indicators.note: in means the eating word sits inside the doorways word

parts.note: entries are ways in, doorways
to eat is to take food, fare

explanation.surface: Passengers pay for their tickets in doorways.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fare' looks like a ticket price but means food, as in good plain fare.
explanation.definitionFit: Earnest pleas or requests are appeals.

clue.text: Get a towel for the medical attendant-that's right!

annotationWithheld.why: 'Get a towel for the medical attendant-that's right! (5)' as OCR'd: DR and R appear but no parse gives the I and E of DRIER; likely misread.
annotationWithheld.clue: Get a towel for the medical attendant-that's right!

clue.text: Member gets through this while dressing

definitions.text: Member gets through this while dressing

parts.words: Member gets through this while dressing
parts.note: a limb, the member, passes through an opening in a garment when you put it on

explanation.surface: Something a club member goes through while getting dressed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Member' looks like a club member but is a limb, the arm.
explanation.definitionFit: The opening in a shirt or coat through which the arm passes is the sleeve hole.

clue.text: Bill and Edward played together

parts.note: ac is short for account, a bill
Ted is a short form of Edward

explanation.surface: Two men named Bill and Edward performed side by side.
explanation.definitionFit: Performed a role on stage, so played a part.

clue.text: Sign for crate, though damaged

indicators.note: damaged means the word crate is broken and its letters reassembled

explanation.surface: A mark left on a crate even though it was damaged.
explanation.definitionFit: A faint mark or vestige left behind is a sign of something.

clue.text: Ring at a certain point to order a cereal

parts.note: a ring is round, the letter O
S is south, a point of the compass

explanation.surface: A phone call at a set time to order breakfast cereal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ring' suggests a telephone call but it is the round letter O; the compass point is S.
explanation.definitionFit: A grain grown for porridge and animal feed is a cereal crop.

clue.text: Pests making the student turn cold

parts.note: L is a learner, a student
to ice is to chill or freeze

explanation.surface: Pests that make a student go cold.
explanation.definitionFit: Small parasitic insects living in hair are pests.

clue.text: Joined in Japanese wedding celebrations

indicators.note: in means the letters lie inside the run of the two words

explanation.surface: Took part in the festivities at a Japanese marriage.
explanation.definitionFit: Stitched together with needle and thread, so joined.

clue.text: A plug for the main trainee social worker

parts.note: the main is a poetic name for the sea
L is a learner, a trainee
the ant is a social insect, often a worker

explanation.surface: A plug for an apprentice welfare officer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Social worker' suggests a welfare officer but is an ant, a social insect; 'plug' is a filler, not publicity.
explanation.definitionFit: A substance that fills and seals a gap or joint is a plug.

clue.text: Uses words with an alternative

indicators.note: alternative means another arrangement of the letters in words and an

explanation.surface: Someone employs words together with a different choice.
explanation.definitionFit: To draw on resources is to make use of them.

clue.text: Protect a woman officer with little hesitation

parts.note: she is the pronoun for a woman
Lt is short for lieutenant, an officer
er is a short hesitant sound

explanation.surface: Guarding a female officer who barely hesitates.
explanation.definitionFit: To shield someone from harm or weather is to protect them.

clue.text: Many will take transport back by ship, given money

parts.note: D is the Roman numeral for 500, many

indicators.note: back means the transport word is read in reverse

parts.note: a car is transport
HMS, His or Her Majesty's Ship, prefixes a ship's name

explanation.surface: Lots of people will ship goods back by sea in return for cash.
explanation.walkthrough: D is 500 in Roman numerals; 'back' turns CAR into RAC; HMS is the Royal Navy ship prefix.
explanation.definitionFit: These were ancient Greek silver coins, a variant of the drachma, so a form of money.

clue.text: Law-breaking article written in Russia

definitions.note: a region located in Russia, as held when the puzzle appeared

parts.note: crime is law-breaking
a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: An item about lawlessness is published in Russia.
explanation.definitionFit: The Black Sea peninsula was then part of the Soviet Union, a region in Russia as the setter saw it.

clue.text: Note and follow report

parts.note: re is the second note of the sol-fa scale
to tail is to follow closely

explanation.surface: Instructions to write something down and then go after a story.
explanation.walkthrough: Besides selling in shops, the answer as a verb means to recount, as in retail gossip.
explanation.definitionFit: To recount a story in detail is to tell or report it.

clue.text: Like the international leader over a lot of land

parts.note: as means like

indicators.note: leader means the first letter of international

explanation.surface: A world leader is compared with something sprawling across a lot of territory.
explanation.definitionFit: The largest continent is a vast expanse of land.

clue.text: This can never include a woman

indicators.note: include means the letters sit within the words can never

explanation.surface: A rule stating that something must never admit a woman.
explanation.definitionFit: A common female forename stands for a woman.

clue.text: Rate fools people in a way

parts.note: asses are fools

indicators.note: in means the people word goes inside the way word

parts.note: St is street, a way
men are people

explanation.surface: Someone ranks fools as people in a certain manner.
explanation.definitionFit: An evaluation or valuation is a rate, as with a local tax rate set by valuation.

clue.text: Points to newspaper leader causing want

parts.note: N is north, a compass point
E is east, another compass point
ed is the editor, who leads a newspaper

explanation.surface: Points made in a newspaper editorial cause hardship.
explanation.definitionFit: Poverty or lack is want, as in living in want.

clue.text: The cost of travelling near &far — it's appalling

indicators.note: appalling means the letters of the words are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: Complaint that travel prices, near and far, are dreadful.
explanation.definitionFit: Ticket prices on the railway are what a journey costs.
